parties: Wipro Limited (acquirer, via step-down subsidiary Wipro IT Services LLC) | Aggne Global IT Services Private Limited (India) and Aggne Global Inc. (US)
headline: Wipro to acquire additional 20% stake in Aggne Global entities
sum: Wipro announced acquisition of an additional 20% stake in Aggne Global IT Services Private Limited and Aggne Global Inc., taking total holding to 80%, with completion expected by 30 June 2026. The transaction follows Wipro's February 2024 acquisition of 60% in both entities through step-down subsidiary Wipro IT Services LLC.
implication: Staged acquisition structures in cross-border IT services deals trigger Reg 30 disclosure duties at each material step; partners must confirm whether remaining 20% minority consent or call provisions exist, and whether any earn-out or deferred consideration is embedded in the seller's non-disclosure.
detail: Wipro Limited, via step-down subsidiary Wipro IT Services LLC, previously acquired 60% of Aggne Global IT Services Private Limited (India entity) and Aggne Global Inc. (US entity) on 14 February 2024. The current announcement (18 June 2026) discloses acquisition of an additional 20%, bringing aggregate holding to 80%, with expected completion by 30 June 2026. The NSE Regulation 30 intimation does not disclose consideration, deal structure, remaining shareholder rights, or any minority put/call mechanisms. The transaction targets a technology services group with India and US operating entities, consistent with Wipro's inorganic M&A strategy in IT services.

framework.ref: SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015, Regulation 30
framework.note: Material acquisition of 20% stake in subsidiary-owned entities triggers disclosure to stock exchange; timing (within 30 min of board/authorized committee approval) and content (parties, value, terms, conditions precedent) must comply.
Acquisition of stake in subsidiary or associated entity may require disclosure of related-party nature and audit committee approval if acquiring entity or target has common management/control.

framework.ref: Foreign Exchange Management Act, 1999 (FEMA), Schedule 7 & RBI Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS)
framework.note: Outbound investment by Indian entity (Wipro) in US-incorporated entity (Aggne Global Inc.) requires RBI approval or compliance with automatic approval routes; step-down subsidiary structure may affect classification.

Acquisition of 20% stake (second tranche) may trigger CCI notification if aggregate deal value exceeds threshold (₹2,000 cr or asset value >₹6,000 cr); staged acquisitions assessed separately or cumulatively depending on control acquisition.

framework.ref: Income Tax Act, 1961, Section 49 (cost basis on acquisition)
framework.note: Step-down subsidiary structure and staged acquisition may affect cost-basis for subsequent sale, depreciation/amortisation claim, and fair-value accounting under Ind AS 103 (Business Combinations).

framework.ref: Wipro Limited By-Laws / Memorandum and Articles of Association
framework.note: Board approval, general authority to subsidiary directors, and disclosure to shareholders (if required by constitution) must be verified; staged acquisition may trigger separate shareholder approval if material.

framework.ref: Schedule 1 and Schedule 2 of Aggne Global entities' incorporation documents (if US LLC / India Pvt Ltd)
framework.note: Minority shareholder rights, tag-along/drag-along provisions, and call/put options on remaining 20% must be reviewed to assess contingent consideration and future squeezeout mechanics.

structure.novel: Staged 60%+20%=80% acquisition structure using step-down subsidiary (Wipro IT Services LLC) in cross-border IT services deal; no earn-out, deferred consideration, or minority protection mechanisms disclosed, suggesting potential acquiree founder/minority exit or lock-in schedule.

triggers.note: Material acquisition disclosure to NSE; second tranche of multi-step buy-in each triggers separate Reg 30 intimation at announcement.
Outbound investment in US entity by Indian parent via subsidiary; route (automatic vs. approval) depends on sector classification and investment amount.
Acquisition of 20% (or cumulative 80%) may trigger CCI combination notification if deal value or target asset base exceeds statutory threshold; staged deals assessed per timing and control transfer.
Step-down acquisition; consolidated group accounting and fair-value measurement of goodwill/intangibles on the second 20% tranche may differ from 60% tranche (non-controlling interest remeasurement).
